speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to narrow down the cause, please describe the onset, whether these lesions are painful or itchy, and if you have any fever or joint pain. Also, have you noticed any rashes on your hands, feet, or buttocks, or any mouth sores prior to the arm blisters?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Fixed Drug Eruption (likely caused by Captopril).

The onset of blisters and mucosal ulcers shortly after starting a new medication (captopril), combined with pain during eating and intercourse, strongly suggests a hypersensitivity reaction. I will request a review of your current medication list and any available skin images to confirm the lesion morphology and rule out other causes like Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
